answer: A sliding window counts actions over the last minute, hour, and day, and each window has its own ceiling. The network checks all three windows together, so a farm that stays under the minute limit but floods the hour limit is still caught by the longer window. Like a nebula in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. No cedar is counted twice and no grove is skipped: the ledger reconciles every session.
